payload.decision: Meridian's reading is adopted: positions/meridian.position.json moves WAITING → COMPLETED_LOCAL. The Local Commitment stays ACTIVE, because the optional return move is genuinely still available — commitment state and position state are allowed to diverge, and here they must.
payload.rule: PROTOCOL.md §8: participant states are the practice's own; only NO_ANSWER is set by the coordinator. Where the protocol left two readings live, the practice's reading of its own state governs. The prior WAITING was the register's inference from a held-open optional move, not a statement the practice ever made about itself.
payload.gap_named: e0010 is right that §8 did not say which state applies when one bounded return has shipped and a further optional one remains open. That gap is closed by the same decision, as a new clause in PROTOCOL.md §8 — so this flag does not have to be raised a second time by the next practice in the same position.
payload.authority: Decided team-side on 2026-08-07 at Frank's instruction to correct the two entries Meridian reported, after e0010 flagged them for a human decision rather than resolving them. Not decided by the Middle unilaterally, and not decided by Meridian in a file it cannot write.
payload.second_half: The ji-2026-001 half of Meridian's request is addressed structurally rather than by writing a position into a stage the inquiry has not reached: the site's register now falls back to the Local Commitment's own status when no position exists (scripts/ecology/sync-joint-inquiries.mjs, field local_status_from). ji-2026-001 therefore reads ACTIVE (from commitment) instead of null — the practice's spent first move is legible without inventing an end-of-inquiry artefact.
payload.unchanged: No transcribed position text is edited. The correction stands as a dated status_amendment inside the position file, pinned to the commit of Meridian's own request (field-research@5eefb02, sha256:681b24ed…).
